HOW MUCH OF THE WAY TOWARD THE BALL THE WHOLE SHAPE SLIDES, 0 to 1. THIS IS WHY A PLAYER OFF THE BALL IS MOVING AT ALL. A real side off the ball is not still and is not fidgeting - it moves as one block, and it moves because the ball moved. 0 holds the shape rigid and puts the aimless wandering back. Past 0.6 the whole side chases the ball and the zones stop meaning anything
HOW MUCH OF THAT SLIDE IS FORWARD AND BACK rather than across, 0 to 1. A line shifts sideways with the ball far more readily than it changes its depth, so this is below half on purpose

HOW FAR A WAITING SIDE LEANS TOWARD THE BALL S END OF THE PITCH, 0 to 1. A defensive line steps up when the ball is in the other half and drops when it comes back. This is a lean, not a chase - 0.16 is a shift of a few metres. 0 holds the shape rigid wherever the ball is

HOW FAR OFF HIS MAN S SHOULDER A MARKER STANDS. THE OTHER ROW THAT STOPPED THE PAIRS. Marking used to be purely goal-side, which put the marker at his man s exact height - two players level, all match. Which shoulder is decided by where the ball is, so a marker shifts as play moves

HOW FAR TOWARD HIS MAN A DEFENDER ACTUALLY COMMITS, 0 to 1. THE ROW THAT DECIDES ZONAL OR MAN MARKING. At 1 a defender follows his man everywhere and the two travel the pitch locked together, which is what made them look glued. At 0.5 the defender s own position is still the bigger half of the decision and his man is a lean on top of it. At 0 he ignores his man entirely and just holds his shape

THE SMALLEST GAP A MARKER MAY END UP AT FROM HIS MAN S EXACT HEIGHT, as a share of mark_shoulder. THE LAST WORD AGAINST A PAIR STANDING PARALLEL. Every other rule here is a lerp or a sum and every one of them can average back to nought - commit half way toward a man a shoulder above you and you are half a shoulder above him, then a drift pointing down puts you level again. This is a floor under all of it. 0 turns it off

HOW FAR PAST HIS MAN THE BALL MUST TRAVEL before a marker switches to the other shoulder, in pixels. The shoulder a defender stands off is decided by where the ball is; without this gap a ball drifting across his man s exact height flips it every frame and the marker jitters. Bigger is calmer and slower to react
HOW FAR A MARKER KEEPS SHIFTING ABOUT on top of the marking spot, in pixels. Nobody in football stands still while marking. 0 parks them
HOW FAR FORWARD A PLAYER BREAKS when showing for the pass, in pixels
HOW FAR TOWARD THEIR OWN TOUCHLINE they break as well. USING THE WIDTH OF THE PITCH. Nobody ever went near a touchline before, so every move went through the middle. 0 keeps play narrow

HOW LONG THE WHOLE PITCH BREAKS TOWARD THE MAN A GOAL KICK IS AIMED AT. His side comes to support, theirs comes to intercept, and they fan out around him rather than piling on the same spot. 0 and everyone stands watching the ball travel, as before

HOW WIDE A SURGING SIDE FANS OUT across the box instead of stacking on the goal mouth, in pixels. surge_centring draws them toward a single point; this pushes them back out to their own share of the width, so a break arrives spread across the area. 0 puts the pile-up back

HOW MANY OF A BREAKING SIDE ACTUALLY RUN INTO THE BOX. THE ROW THAT STOPPED THE HUDDLE AT THE SHOT. Every player used to close the same fraction of the distance to the same goal mouth, which is ten people converging on one point. Now the three nearest the goal attack DIFFERENT stations - near post, far post, the spot, the edge - and everybody else pushes up and holds the shape. 0 means nobody goes and the shot arrives out of nowhere; 10 puts the heap back
HOW MUCH OF THE RUNNERS ADVANCE THE PLAYERS HOLDING THE SHAPE MAKE, 0 to 1. They are the reason there is somebody to pass back to, so they push up without following the ball into the area

HOW MANY DEFENDERS GO AND CLOSE THE BALL DOWN while the other side breaks. The rest drop off, stay goal-side and keep the distance between them. Every defender used to snap onto a man dead level with him the instant a break started, which was the glued look at its worst at the one moment you are certain to be watching

HOW FAR A PLAYER MAY WANDER FROM THEIR SLOT, as a fraction of their roam band. THE CAGE NOBODY WAS BLAMING. The leash used to be a flat 210 pixels whatever the size of the pitch, which is less than half a quarter - a player could not reach the edge of their OWN zone, never mind anybody else s. As a fraction it scales with the pitch and with zone_roam. A player chasing the ball ignores the leash completely
false returns to the old layout - both squads in their own half, no quarters, no marking
Fraction of the pitch each Tier owns outright

HOW MUCH OF THE PITCH A TIER MOVES ABOUT IN FREELY, as a fraction of the width. This is NOT a fence - nothing is ever stopped at its edge. Inside this band nothing pulls a player back at all; outside it there is a gentle tug home, and a player chasing the ball ignores even that. 0.6 means the bands overlap heavily, which is what a formation looks like. Raise it towards 1 and the shape loosens; drop it to 0.3 and you are back to four cages

HOW WIDE A BAND A TIER TREATS A LOOSE BALL AS ITS OWN JOB, as a fraction of the pitch. NOT the same question as zone_roam, and running the two together is what made the midfield heap: roam is 60% of the pitch because nothing should drag a player back from most of the grass, but if every Tier also CLAIMS everything inside 60% then a ball on the centre spot belongs to four Tiers at once and six players set off for it. Raise it and more players converge on every loose ball; drop it toward zone_share and each Tier only answers for its own quarter
